title: 돌려서 말하기: 진짜 뜻은 뭘까요?
objective: By the end, you can read an indirect Korean line and tell whether it is a soft refusal, a hidden request, or a polite sign to finish.
summary: This worksheet shows common Korean phrases that refuse, ask, or disagree indirectly, and what they really mean.
note: These phrases are common in everyday Korean, but tone and situation always decide the real meaning.

task.title: Find the real meaning
task.line: Read each Korean line and decide what the speaker really means, wants, or should say.

sections.heading: Why Koreans often say it the long way
paragraphs: In Korean, a plain 'no' such as 안 돼요 or 싫어요 can sound cold, especially to older people, coworkers, or new friends. So people often refuse, ask, or disagree in a roundabout way. The listener is expected to find the real meaning from the situation.

In Korean, lines like 'I'll think about it' or 'Let's eat sometime' are often not meant literally. When someone answers a request or invitation, watch for these clues: 좀, -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요, a sentence that stops in the middle (...), or a reason with no clear answer. Together they often mean 'no'.

items.text: Often a polite 'no', especially to a sales offer or an invitation.
A soft way to say 'I can't do it.'
Stopping in the middle tells the listener the answer is no.
When someone offers something, it often means 'no, thanks', not 'good'.
A friendly goodbye; it is usually not a real plan with a date.
items.example: 오늘 반가웠어요. 다음에 밥 한번 먹어요.

items.text: Opens a question or request softly.
A cushion you say before asking for help.
items.example: 바쁘신데 죄송하지만, 이것 좀 봐 주실 수 있어요?

items.text: A question about the room that is really a request, like closing a window.
items.example: 창문이 열려 있네요. 좀 춥지 않아요?

items.text: Shows you disagree or don't like an idea without saying why.
items.example: 회의를 일요일에 해요? 그건 좀 그렇네요.

items.text: A polite sign that you want to finish or leave.
items.example: 어머, 시간이 벌써 이렇게 됐네요. 슬슬 일어날까요?

sections.heading: How to refuse an invitation softly

exercises: Read the message. What does 민지 really mean? (a) She probably won't come. (b) She will surely come.: 토요일 모임이요? 그날은 일이 좀 있어서요. 일단 생각해 볼게요.
Is the speaker asking you to do something? Write Yes or No: ① (at night, in your room) 이 방이 좀 어둡네요. ② 주말에 본 영화가 정말 재미있었어요. ③ (at a bank counter) 아, 펜을 안 가져왔네요...
Fill in the blank with a soft refusal using -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요: 죄송하지만 이번 주는 바빠서 같이 가기는 ____.
Put the sentences in order, following the steps in 'How to refuse an invitation softly': (A) 다음 달에는 꼭 갈게요. (B) 초대해 줘서 고마워요. (C) 그날 부모님이 오셔서요. (D) 이번에는 좀 힘들 것 같아요.
At a team dinner, your manager says this. What does the manager really want? (a) to order more food (b) to end the dinner: 다들 내일 일찍 출근해야 하죠? 오늘 정말 즐거웠어요.
answers: ① Yes (turn on the light) ② No ③ Yes (lend a pen)
어려울 것 같아요 (좀 어려울 것 같아요 / 힘들 것 같아요)
